full_judgment: 3. Mr Md Nawab AJi, Advocate-on-Record, appeared on behalf of the appellants. He has taken us through the first information report, the deposition of the witnesses, judgment of the trial Court and judgment of the High Court Division. He has submitted that though six witnesses were examined in support of the prosecution case, not a single witness supported the prosecution case. He has specifically given emphasis on the fact that the victim herself and her mother did not support the prosecution case. As regards PW 1, the informant, the learned Advocate further submits that the evidence of PW 1 is merely hearsay evidence because he did not see the occurrence and he only heard about the occurrence from Manik and his daughter Parul, the victim. Next, he has submitted that the High Court Division and also the trial Court wrongly admitted into evidence the statement of victim which was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the medical report of doctor who examined the victim after the occurrence. He has argued that both the courts erred in law in finding the appellants guilty relying on inadmissible evidence, that is the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and medical report. Lastly, he has submitted that the findings of the High Court Division and also of the trial Court are merely based on surmise and conjecture and, as such, conviction is not supported by the evidence on record.
